Huntley College of Agriculture College of Business Administration College of Education and Integrative Studies College of Engineering College of Environmental Design College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences College of Science The Collins College of Hospitality Management College of Professional and Global Education University Library Student Programs for Support and Enrichment Centers and Institutes University Interdisciplinary Programs Index of Courses Index of Academic Programs Index of Roadmaps Index of Academic Colleges, Departments, and Programs University Administration, Regulations, and History Directory Archived Catalog PDFs My Portfolio Add to My Favorites (opens a new window) Share this Page Facebook this Page (opens a new window) Tweet this Page (opens a new window) Print (opens a new window) Help (opens a new window) 2026-2027 University Catalog Art Department Building 13 Room 2113 | (909) 869-3508 | Department Website | Faculty Directory Through teaching excellence and program quality the Department of Art continues to align itself with the University mission to cultivate success through a diverse culture of experiential learning, discovery, and innovation. The department is dedicated to creativity, environmental and social awareness, and ethical design practices. Building on these values, the Department of Art-offering a B.F.A. in Visual Communication Design and a B.A. in Art History-is fully accredited by NASAD and emphasizes Cal Poly Pomona’s signature “learn-by-doing” approach. In design studios and art history lectures and seminars, students engage with environmental and ethical issues through hands-on projects, research collaboration, and service learning. Department faculty are active practitioners and scholars whose work enriches curriculum relevance and professional rigor. The Visual Communication Design program is noted for its regional standing-including rankings among California’s top design schools-and Art History is noted for its award-winning faculty. Student engagement is central: visual design majors participate in juried exhibitions, an annual industry showcase, and internships with leading LA-area firms. Student organizations such as AIGA‑CPP facilitate industry connections through speaker events, portfolio reviews, and competitions. Art History students contribute to departmental newsletters, archival projects, and mentoring. Rigorous advising, studio critique culture, digital fabrication labs, and access to galleries like Kellogg University Art Gallery round out

courses.title: World Art: Prehistory through Medieval Europe
courses.description: [GE 3A] Comprehensive survey and analysis of the development of art in ancient civilizations from prehistoric times through the Middle Ages (ca. 30,000 BCE through 14th century).
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Art: Renaissance through Modern Europe and the United States
courses.description: [GE 3A] Comprehensive survey and analysis of the development of art in Western civilization from the Renaissance through the modern period in Europe and the United States (ca. 15th through 20th centuries).
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Art: Asia (Prehistory to 12th Century)
courses.description: [GE 3A] Comprehensive survey of art, architecture, and material culture of India, Southeast Asia, China, Korea and Japan from prehistory to the 12th century. Emphasis on historical and religious contexts.
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: World Art: Africa, Oceania, and Native America
courses.description: [GE 3A] Study of the visual and material culture of selected civilizations and cultures within Africa, Oceania, and the Americas in relation to belief systems and social functions.
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Art of Ancient Egypt and the Near East
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of ancient civilizations, primarily Egypt and Mesopotamia, showing the interrelations and cultural exchanges of the ancient world.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art of the Classical World
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of the Western classical world; the development of Greek, Etruscan, and Roman art.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art of the Middle Ages
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of art and architecture of the European Middle Ages, from early Christian art through late Gothic.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art of the Italian Renaissance
courses.description: Survey of art and architecture of Italy of the 14th through 16th centuries.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art in the Age of the Baroque
courses.description: Survey of art and architecture of the 17th and 18th centuries in Northern and Southern Europe.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art of the United States
courses.description: Survey of the art of the United States from the art of the colonies to the key role of American artists in the development of modern art.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: History of Design
courses.description: A trans-disciplinary, international survey of major developments in visual and spatial aesthetic design from industrialization to the present. Design trends are studied as products of larger transformations in commerce and culture. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Modernism in Visual Art
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the founding movements and key developments in the history of modernism and the avant-garde in Europe and the United States from the late nineteenth century through the mid-twentieth century.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Contemporary Art
courses.description: Survey and analysis of international trends in visual art since the 1960s with special emphasis on the current scene.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art and Architecture of India
courses.description: Comprehensive survey of the art and architecture of the Indian subcontinent. Focuses on the religious traditions of India and their role in the production of architecture and visual imagery from the Indus Valley Civilization to the Mughal Empire.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Arts of Korea
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of Korea from Neolithic times to the 19th century.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Arts of Japan
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of Japan from Neolithic times to the 19th century. Emphasis on Buddhist art.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Arts of China
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of China from prehistory through the Manchu domination of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing. AH 2303 is recommended (not required).

courses.title: Arts of Native America
courses.description: Comprehensive survey and analysis of the arts of Native North America from Precontact, Historic and Modern/Contemporary time (c.1100BCE to present time).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing. AH 2305 recommended (not required).

courses.title: Arts of Mexico, Central and South America
courses.description: Art and material culture from pre-Columbian civilizations in ancient Mexico, Central and South America (from prehistoric times through the 15th century).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Art History Internship
courses.description: On-the-job training in an on-campus gallery, archive, or special collection, such as the W. Keith & Janet Kellogg Art Gallery or the University Library Special Collections and Archives. University and Department internship guidelines must be followed, coordinated with the gallery or archive supervisor, and approved in advance by the department internship coordinator. Students must interview with the gallery or archive supervisor and be approved for in the internship before receiving department permission to enroll. This course is not available for off-campus internships.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of department/instructor and supervisor; and C- or better in two of the following: AH 2301 , AH 2302 , AH 2303 , or AH 2305 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 8 units

courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Intensive, guided research seminar to develop and master Art History research and writing skills. Topics may vary.
courses.prerequisites: Any 3 of the following: AH 2301 , AH 2302 , AH 2303 , or AH 2305 with C- or better; any 2 upper-division AH courses with C- or better; and AH 3300 with C- or better; junior or senior standing; B.A. in Art History major; or permission of instructor.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Introduction to art historical methodologies, development of skills of research and writing. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Art History major and senior standing.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Cumulative course incorporates demonstrating mastery of skills necessary for proficiency in the Art History major and relevant careers by independently researching, writing, and presenting an original argument.

courses.title: Foundations in Drawing 1 Activity
courses.description: Study of drawing with emphasis on depictive concepts, materials, tools, and techniques. Basic mechanical drawing techniques and interpretations are introduced. Emphasis on development of perception, concepts and methods.

courses.title: Foundations in Drawing 2 Activity
courses.description: A synthesis of the basic drawing elements (line, value, texture, composition) and perspective with an imaginative and self-expressive use of material. Skills and techniques in drawing the human figure from studio models.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A .

courses.title: Foundations in 2D Design Activity
courses.description: Development of appreciative and creative skills. Variety of materials used, with an emphasis on two-dimensional design concepts, especially color theory, typography, and visual perception.

courses.title: Foundations in Ceramics Activity
courses.description: [GE 3A] Methods and procedures for pottery making techniques emphasizing the use of the pottery wheel and functional vessels. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: Non-Visual Communication Design or non-Graphic Design Major.

courses.title: Foundations in 3D Design Activity
courses.description: An introduction to and exploration of the elements and principles of three-dimensional design and their applications, with emphasis on form in space, design systems, and contemporary art concepts.

courses.title: Foundations in 4D Design Activity
courses.description: An introduction to, and exploration of, the visual elements and their principles in four dimensional design-visual design that is sequential and happens in a given amount time using motion-and subsequent applications, with an emphasis of movement of form in design systems and contemporary art concepts.

courses.title: Foundations in 5D Design Activity
courses.description: An introduction to and exploration of User Experience and User Interaction (UX/UI) and application to web design, technology, and acuity with an understanding of linear and non-linear sequencing. Technical knowledge will include traditional technology within the field, web publishing platforms, basics of HTML coding, CSS, web development software, and image editing applications.

courses.title: Typography Activity
courses.description: A hands-on introduction to the elements of typography. Development of appreciation and skillful usage of typographic elements in two, three, and four dimensions.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1312A , VCD 1321A , VCD 1331A , VCD 1341A , and VCD 1351A .

courses.title: Illustration Activity
courses.description: Developing graphic images with an individual voice. Emphasis on innovation and conceptual thinking through varied illustrative media and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1312A , VCD 1321A , VCD 1331A , VCD 1341A , and VCD 1351A.

courses.title: Visual Communication Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Application of 2D, 3D, 4D, and 5D design principles in visual communication with an introduction to design process, methodology/theory and problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1312A , VCD 1321A , VCD 1331A , VCD 1341A , and VCD 1351A.

courses.title: Digital Photography Activity
courses.description: Explore the technical and aesthetic aspects of digital photography, including effective utilization of cameras, software, and digital output in the creation of photographic work, including photographic work needed in graphic design portfolios.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A , VCD 1321A , and VCD 1331A .

courses.title: Visual Thinking
courses.description: Promotion of conceptual development, investigations in principles of visual organization, color, and design and critical analysis of the context in which visual information appears. Cultivate the ability to interpret different kinds of signs associated with the field of image making. A wide range of approaches and media will be studied to develop greater perceptual and conceptual awareness and understanding.

courses.title: Studio Arts: Life Drawing Activity
courses.description: Drawing for creative expression from studio models using a variety of drawing materials at an advanced level. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A , VCD 1321A, and VCD 1331A .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 6 units.

courses.description: Traditional and non-traditional painting methods and subject matter explored to develop the students’ ability to express themselves in varied media.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A , VCD 1321A , and VCD 1331A .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 6 units.

courses.description: A study of methods and techniques for historical and contemporary studio print processes such as relief, intaglio, monotype, letterpress, and screen printing, and their application to visual communication design. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A , VCD 1321A , and VCD 1331A .

courses.description: Technical construction of three-dimensional clay. Define ceramic history, safe clay studio management, load and unload kilns, and glaze calculation. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 1311A , VCD 1321A , and VCD 1331A .

courses.title: Workshop: Typography
courses.description: Advanced study of normative typography and an in-depth exploration of typographic nomenclature, its application to live copy, grid systems, and complex hierarchy across a variety of mediums in 2D, 3D, 4D, and 5D.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Workshop: Illustration
courses.description: Advanced study in the creation of contemporary, commercial illustration and further explores the computer as an illustrative medium. Idea development within real-world parameters, originality, aesthetics, and technical proficiency are emphasized.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Workshop: 2D
courses.description: Advanced study in print processes, identity systems, and serial print communications in publication, editorial, and book design.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Workshop: 3D
courses.description: Advanced study of visual communication design in three-dimensional applications in branding of products and reinforcing the sense of place.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Workshop: 4D
courses.description: Advanced study of time-based media and motion using technology within the field. Emphasis is on acuity to and the creation of motion as may be used in visual communications.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Workshop: 5D
courses.description: Advanced study of User Experience and User Interaction (UX/UI) and application to design, technology, and acuity with a comprehensive understanding of experimental processes, techniques and methodology found therein.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2301A , VCD 2311A , VCD 2321A , VCD 2361A , and VCD 2370 .

courses.title: Visual Communication Design: Internship
courses.description: On-the-job training in visual communication design. University and department internship guidelines must be followed, coordinated with sponsor, and approved in advance by the department internship coordinator. One unit of credit is given for 50 or more hours of training visual communication design professional.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 2321A , VCD major with junior or senior standing, and consent of instructor required.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 8 units.

courses.title: Professional Practices in Visual Communication Design
courses.description: A capstone course for senior visual communication design in which a professional portfolio is developed. Professional business practices are thoroughly discussed and reviewed.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in VCD 3321A .
